A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RESCUE study, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures throughout. Both end with references; neither includes an appendix or the separate supplementary document mentioned in the text.

before.justification: v1 reports original evacuation simulations, including success rates and fall counts in Table 2, component ablations, speed distributions, and density and terrain analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation results in Table 2 and Figures 4-9, including comparisons, ablations, and evacuation analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2-3.5 retain the same SDM loop, personalized SFM with evasive forces, PACER/CAMDM gait controller, training loss, upper-body action replacement, and part-level force visualization.

E1.justification: Both use 100STYLE and the same evacuation scenarios, five personalized population groups, crowd densities, corridor widths, and normal, uneven, obstacle-covered, and slippery terrain conditions.

E2.justification: SFM, OmniControl, and MaskedMimic remain the qualitative comparators; Table 2 retains OmniControl and MaskedMimic. Removing both proposed components still yields the PACER ablation baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 retains four scenes, 50 agents per scene, 1000 frames, and average escape success and fall-count metrics. The speed-diversity, crowd-density, corridor-width, and terrain experiment settings also match.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Figure 6, speed-diversity analysis in Figure 7, density and corridor-width analysis in Figure 8, and terrain tests in Figure 9 are retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Both specify 10 runs per scene in Section 4.2 and show the same speed-distribution boxplot. Neither adds seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Table 2 retains success rates of 0.48 for OmniControl, 0.60 for MaskedMimic, and 0.84 for RESCUE, with fall counts of 18.55 and 12.26 for the latter two. The graphical results and qualitative findings also match.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(4) retain the same evasive-force definition, velocity update, diffusion prediction, and weighted loss. Gait-phase definitions are unchanged, and no proofs or theoretical results are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about online personalized 3D evacuation, SDM integration, force visualization, realism, and applicability. The proposed contributions and their scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: The introduction changes the statement that existing character controllers 'thus result in' falls and collisions to 'may result in,' modestly qualifying the causal assertion. Interpretations of the experimental findings and applicability boundaries otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Calibration tolerance, gait matching and augmentation instructions, baseline adaptations, and the code-availability statement are unchanged. Moving a supplementary-materials pointer within Section 3.4 adds no implementation information.

R1.justification: The same 50 cited works, related-work categories, and novelty positioning are retained. Expanded reference author lists and capitalization changes are bibliographic edits rather than additions to the literature coverage.

P1.justification: v2 makes scattered grammar and terminology edits, such as 'we proposes' to 'we propose,' moves a supplementary-reference sentence, and expands bibliography author names. Section order and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The same nine figures and two tables retain their content and structure. Text reflow shifts several figures and Table 2, Figure 3 gains caption punctuation, and expanded references occupy more of the final page.

improvement.justification: v2 provides modest editorial gains through grammar corrections, fuller reference attribution, and qualification of the categorical statement about prior controllers causing falls. The method, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited to presentation and precision.
